articles.title: How to Train a Critic Stably and Efficiently
articles.summary: Group-based reinforcement learning methods such as GRPO for large language models avoid training a critic by sampling multiple responses for each prompt. A reliable critic could instead estimate token-level advantages from one response, but standard critic-based training recipes are often unstable. articles.title: ReWorld: An Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory
articles.summary: An interactive world model must follow the user's actions, remember the places it has shown, and stream in real time. The tension is structural: control wants a short horizon, memory wants an unbounded one. ReWorld separates the two during training and bounds them at inference. articles.title: SWE Refactor Bench: Can Coding Agents Complete a Long-Horizon, Whole-Repository Stack Migration?
articles.summary: Modern software systems accumulate technical debt over decades of development, which makes migration expensive and largely manual. As coding agents become increasingly capable at bug fixing, can they autonomously perform such migrations? Existing benchmarks cannot answer this question because they evaluate only behavioural correctness, not whether the migration actually occurred. articles.title: EG-ARSA: An Expert-Grounded Open Model for Visual Road Safety Auditing in Low-Resource Settings
articles.summary: Road traffic injuries remain a major challenge in low- and middle-income countries, where proactive road safety auditing is limited by incomplete crash records, shortages of qualified auditors, and the high cost of large-scale field inspections. articles.title: The descendants of $z \gtrsim 10$ JWST galaxies in the COLIBRE simulations
articles.summary: Recent observations with JWST have revealed a population of UV-bright galaxies at $z\gtrsim 10$. This discovery naturally raises the question: what do such early galaxies evolve into by the present day? In this work, we address this descendant question using the new-generation COLIBRE cosmological hydrodynamical simulations to trace bright galaxies selected at $z=10$ and follow their descendants to the present day. articles.title: Two-loop renormalisation and Higgs phenomenology in the five-dimensional MSSM
articles.summary: The five-dimensional Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (5D MSSM) provides an attractive framework in which power-law renormalisation group evolution naturally generates a sizeable trilinear stop coupling, allowing the observed Higgs boson mass to be reproduced without requiring too heavy a supersymmetric spectra. articles.title: Provably adaptive sampling with uniform and remasking discrete diffusion models
articles.summary: Discrete diffusion models offer a promising alternative to autoregressive generation by enabling parallel updates, but their sampling efficiency can depend strongly on the choice of the forward process and the sampler. articles.title: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
articles.summary: Language models are sequential processors, but long-horizon agency requires external information and computation beyond model weights and active context. Prime Agent is an open-source harness for long-horizon evaluation and coding-agent workflows. articles.summary: Recent advances in continuous diffusion and flow-based language models (LMs) have achieved performance competitive with discrete LMs. However, existing continuous frameworks still rely on decoders supervised with cross entropy (CE) because the flow trajectories are not guaranteed to terminate at valid token embeddings. articles.title: When "Do Not" Is Not Deny: Security Rules in CLAUDE.md vs Built-In Controls
articles.summary: In CLAUDE.md, "do not" is a natural-language instruction that the model interprets. Claude Code's deny is a built-in control that blocks an action before the agent can take it. articles.summary: Rendering views using 3D scene representations such as Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF), meshes, or even point clouds produces artifacts when input views are sparse or target views lie far from the input. articles.summary: Atmospheric photochemical models incorporating the impacts of stellar flares often assume a $\sim$9,000 K spectrum at ultraviolet-optical wavelengths. articles.title: Robustness of Anomaly Detection Models for Industrial Control Systems under Training-Time Data Contamination
articles.summary: Machine-learning-based anomaly detection is increasingly used in industrial control systems (ICS), yet most studies assume that detector training data is trustworthy. In practice, training data may be corrupted through compromised logs, labeling errors, manipulated historian records, or unsafe retraining processes. articles.title: How AI Assistance Affects Human Skill Development: A Study of Learning with Logic Puzzles
articles.summary: While AI assistance can improve human task performance in the short term, it may also undermine the development of skills in the longer term. We examine this tension in a controlled logic-puzzle experiment involving on-demand AI assistance, where participants complete tasks before, during, and after AI is available. articles.title: Interpretable AI with Local Distillation
articles.summary: Modern AI models such as tabular foundation models and gradient-boosted ensembles can outpredict classical methods, but provide little basis for reasoning about their predictions. High-stakes decisions call for models that are both accurate and interpretable as built. articles.title: Adapter-Based Few-Shot Continual Learning for Malicious Packet Recognition
articles.summary: The continual evolution of malware variants necessitates detection systems that can adapt to new threats without retraining from scratch. articles.title: Bound States in Exactly Solvable Polaritonic Models
articles.summary: We study a one-dimensional scalar model for an effective-mass quasiparticle field coupled to a continuum of two-level atoms with at most one excitation present. articles.summary: Massive stars characteristically form in clustered environments. articles.summary: World models can predict video without learning dynamics that they reliably preserve. articles.title: EarthVerse: Benchmarking Scientific Agents Across Dynamic Earth Systems and Natural Hazards
articles.summary: Earth-system analysis reconstructs changing physical processes from observations that differ in source, scale, timing, and modality. Natural hazards make this work consequential because incomplete evidence can change estimates of severity, exposure, and mechanism. articles.title: The Measurement Revolution? Credible Measurement and Inference in the Age of AI
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming measurement in economics. AI models convert unstructured data, such as text and images, into structured variables at low cost, making previously prohibitive measurement feasible at scale. articles.summary: Run-and-tumble particles (RTPs) are canonically modeled with uniform reorientation probabilities, an assumption that breaks down for many biological microswimmers. articles.summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) achieve strong performance in visual reasoning tasks, but it remains unclear whether they understand visual relations, or simply employ shortcuts such as language cues or priors. articles.summary: Extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) spectroscopy represents an important new direction in precision physics, with potential applications ranging from the metrology of fundamental constants to tests of physics beyond the Standard Model. articles.title: Asymptotics for Model Selection in Probabilistic Principal Component Analysis
articles.summary: The probabilistic formulation of principal component analysis promises statistically grounded solutions to the problem of selecting the number of principal components. articles.summary: Probability density functions are commonly estimated through preliminary smoothing or aggregation procedures, e.g., histograms or kernel density estimation, before subsequent functional representation and functional data analyses. articles.summary: Earth System Models (ESMs) rely heavily on High-Performance Computing (HPC) resources to simulate global climate. articles.summary: In panels with sample selection (that may occur due to attrition, nonresponse, etc.), the assumption of selection on observables (missing at random, MAR) is commonly imposed despite often being implausible. articles.summary: We investigate how cosmological environment regulates the evolution of primordial black hole (PBH) seeds in the early universe using a suite of hydrodynamical simulations.
